company: Vicinity Centres (the stapled group of Vicinity Limited and Vicinity Centres Trust, of which Vicinity Centres RE Ltd is the responsible entity)
title: Securities Trading Policy (Version 9)
date_next_review: Every two years, or earlier if deemed necessary (i.e. by 1 September 2027); material amendments approved by the Risk, Compliance and ESG Committee

tiers.name: directors and employees
tiers.description: All directors and employees of Vicinity, where employee includes casual, temporary and permanent staff, and consultants, secondees or contractors in an employment like relationship. Bound by the insider trading prohibition and the blackout periods, but not by the approval requirements or the section 8 hedging, speculative dealing and margin lending prohibitions. The Policy also applies to employees on extended leave.

tiers.name: Restricted Officers
tiers.description: Directors; members of the Executive Leadership Team and the Vicinity Leadership Group; team members titled General Manager, Regional General Manager or Head of; Company Secretariat, Investor Relations & Corporate Communications, Strategy and Corporate Finance, Treasury, Legal Counsel, Property Investment Analytics, Group Financial Planning & Analysis, Group Property Insights and Capital Transactions team members; any direct report of an Executive Leadership Team member including executive and personal assistants; and anyone designated for a specific duration by the CEO, Chief Legal, Risk & ESG Officer or CFO. A reference to Restricted Officers is also a reference to their Close Associates.

tiers.name: Chairman
tiers.description: Distinguished only for approval: may deal only after prior consultation with and approval from both the Chairman of the Audit Committee and the CEO.

tiers.name: Other Directors
tiers.description: Distinguished only for approval: may deal only after prior consultation with and approval from both the Chairman of the Board and the CEO. Their dealings are reported to ASX by the Company Secretary.

tiers.name: CEO
tiers.description: The Chief Executive Officer & Managing Director; may deal only after prior consultation with and approval from both the Chairman of the Board and the Chief Legal, Risk & ESG Officer or Group Company Secretary. The CEO is also an approver for other Restricted Officers and may impose ad hoc trading restrictions with the Chief Legal, Risk & ESG Officer.

tiers.name: All other Restricted Officers
tiers.description: Restricted Officers below Board and CEO level; may deal only after prior approval by any two of the CEO, Chief Legal, Risk & ESG Officer or the Group Company Secretary, except for a transfer out of an employee share plan trust account with no change in beneficial ownership.

tiers.name: Close Associates
tiers.description: Spouse, partner or dependent children (including dependent adult and step-children); any trustee of a trust or other fiduciary arrangement under which the Restricted Officer, their spouse or partner or their dependent children are or may be a beneficiary; and any company in which the Restricted Officer or those persons directly or indirectly holds a majority of the shares or otherwise controls or significantly influences. They are subject to the approval requirements and the section 8 prohibitions in their own right.

definitions.hedging_definition: hedging or entering into an arrangement that would have the effect of limiting their exposure to risk relating to an element of their remuneration that is unvested, or which remains subject to a trading restriction or forfeiture condition

windows.start_anchor: market close at the end of VCX's financial half-year (31 December)
windows.end_anchor: the beginning of trading on the trading day after the announcement of VCX's half-yearly financial results

windows.start_anchor: market close at the end of VCX's financial year (30 June)
windows.end_anchor: the beginning of trading on the trading day after the announcement of VCX's annual financial results

windows.start_anchor: any extension of a blackout period, or any other period during which the directors impose restrictions on trading, as determined by the Chairman of the Board or the CEO in consultation with the Chief Legal, Risk & ESG Officer

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The directors reserve the right to impose restrictions on trading during any other periods; such a determination may be made by the Chairman of the Board or the CEO in consultation with the Chief Legal, Risk & ESG Officer. Blackout periods are not confidential: directors and employees are notified of their commencement and conclusion by email. Separately, the CEO, Chief Legal, Risk & ESG Officer or CFO may designate any employee a Restricted Officer for a specified duration.

rules.detail: There is no separate derivatives rule, but 'VCX securities' is defined to include any derivatives entered into with a third party over or in relation to any VCX securities, which squarely captures an OTC put and call written by a bank. Dealing in them therefore requires the dual approvals in clause 4.2 and is barred during blackout periods.
rules.evidence: VCX securities: Any Securities of Vicinity Centres and any derivatives entered into with a third party over or in relation to any VCX securities.

rules.detail: Directors and employees who are not Restricted Officers need no approval, but because OTC derivatives are VCX securities they may not enter, close or vary them during a blackout period, and never while in possession of inside information.
rules.evidence: Directors and employees may not deal, nor may they procure any other person to deal (including by giving hints or tips to that person), in VCX securities in any capacity

rules.detail: Absolute ban, with no approval route, on hedging or any arrangement limiting exposure to risk relating to an element of remuneration that is unvested. Extends to Close Associates.
rules.evidence: Restricted Officers and their Close Associates are prohibited from: ... hedging or entering into an arrangement that would have the effect of limiting their exposure to risk relating to an element of their remuneration that is unvested, or which remains subject to a trading restriction or forfeiture condition

rules.detail: The same absolute ban reaches remuneration that has vested but remains subject to a trading restriction or forfeiture condition, so a collar cannot be written over holding-locked or clawback-exposed plan securities.
rules.evidence: an element of their remuneration that is unvested, or which remains subject to a trading restriction or forfeiture condition

rules.detail: The hedging prohibition is tied to elements of remuneration that are unvested, restricted or forfeitable, so it does not reach shares that have vested free of restriction or were bought on market. Hedging those is not prohibited, but the derivative legs are VCX securities, so a Restricted Officer needs the clause 4.2 approvals and must act outside a blackout period.
rules.evidence: Restricted Officers and their Close Associates may only deal in VCX securities after prior consultation with and approval by the appropriate persons

rules.detail: Section 8 binds only Restricted Officers and their Close Associates; hedging by other directors and employees is not addressed, though any derivative is a VCX security subject to the blackout periods.

Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward or collar-plus-loan over unrestricted vested securities is a dealing in VCX securities (as a third-party derivative) requiring the clause 4.2 approvals, and is not caught by the section 8 prohibitions unless it is properly described as a margin lending arrangement or takes a security interest over restricted vested securities. Over unvested or restricted remuneration it is prohibited outright.
rules.evidence: any derivatives entered into with a third party over or in relation to any VCX securities

rules.detail: Short selling is named as a form of prohibited speculative dealing, with no approval route, and extends to Close Associates.
rules.evidence: engaging in speculative dealing in VCX securities, being short-selling VCX securities and short-term dealing

rules.detail: The speculative dealing prohibition in section 8 is addressed only to Restricted Officers and their Close Associates.

Securities lending is not named anywhere in the Policy and there is no definition of dealing that would sweep it in, although lending stock to support a short position would engage the short-selling prohibition.

CFDs are not named. A CFD is a derivative entered into with a third party in relation to VCX securities and so a VCX security requiring clause 4.2 approvals, but a short CFD would breach the short-selling prohibition and one closed within 30 days would breach the short-term dealing prohibition, so approval is unlikely in practice.
rules.evidence: any derivatives entered into with a third party over or in relation to any VCX securities

rules.detail: Outright ban with no approval route on arrangements properly described as margin lending arrangements in relation to VCX securities, expressly including entering into one, transferring VCX securities into an existing margin loan account and selling VCX securities held in such an account. Because the sale limb is prohibited rather than merely gated, a margin call sale is a breach rather than a clearance question.
rules.evidence: entering into arrangements properly described as margin lending arrangements in relation to VCX securities, which may include entering into a margin lending arrangement in respect of VCX securities, transferring VCX securities into an existing margin loan account and selling VCX securities held in an existing margin loan account.

rules.detail: The margin lending prohibition in section 8 binds only Restricted Officers and their Close Associates.
Any financial arrangement granting a security interest over vested VCX securities that remain subject to a trading restriction or forfeiture condition is banned outright, with no approval route.
rules.evidence: entering into any financial arrangements whereby a security interest is granted in respect of any vested VCX Securities which remain subject to a trading restriction or forfeiture condition

rules.detail: The security interest prohibition is deliberately confined to vested securities that remain subject to a trading restriction or forfeiture condition, so granting security over freely held vested securities is not prohibited. Granting a security interest is not itself characterised as dealing, so on the face of the Policy it does not even require clause 4.2 approval, though prudence and the reputational factor in clause 4.3.3 point to seeking it.
rules.evidence: entering into any financial arrangements whereby a security interest is granted in respect of any vested VCX Securities which remain subject to a trading restriction or forfeiture condition

rules.detail: Curiously the security interest prohibition names only vested securities, so granting security over unvested entitlements is not expressly addressed; in practice unvested plan entitlements are not capable of being charged and any arrangement limiting risk on them is banned by the hedging limb.

The Policy has no general secured financing prohibition. A bespoke bank facility secured on unrestricted vested VCX securities is caught only if it is 'properly described as a margin lending arrangement', which a bilateral term loan with a fixed advance and no maintenance margin ordinarily is not. The absence of any forced-sale exclusion means lender enforcement during a blackout would nonetheless be a dealing in breach of section 3.
rules.evidence: entering into arrangements properly described as margin lending arrangements in relation to VCX securities

rules.detail: Financing secured on vested securities that remain subject to a trading restriction or forfeiture condition is banned outright by the security interest limb, whatever the form of the facility.
rules.evidence: entering into any financial arrangements whereby a security interest is granted in respect of any vested VCX Securities which remain subject to a trading restriction or forfeiture condition

rules.detail: Section 8 binds only Restricted Officers and their Close Associates; secured financing by other directors and employees is not addressed.

A 30-day round-trip test, applying in both directions (buy then sell, or sell then buy) and across any VCX securities rather than the same parcel. Because VCX securities include third-party derivatives, opening and closing a derivative position within 30 days, or dealing in shares within 30 days of an option leg, is caught. There is no carve-out for shares acquired on vesting.
rules.evidence: short-term dealing (i.e. if a person buys (or sells) VCX securities on a date and then sells (or buys) any VCX securities on a date that is less than 30 days after the first dealing)

rules.detail: The short-term dealing prohibition applies only to Restricted Officers and their Close Associates.

short_term.evidence: short-term dealing (i.e. if a person buys (or sells) VCX securities on a date and then sells (or buys) any VCX securities on a date that is less than 30 days after the first dealing)

exemption_authority: Section 6 permits blackout period trading in exceptional circumstances (significant personal financial hardship where sale is the only reasonable course of action, a court order or court enforceable undertaking, or an overriding legal or regulatory requirement), approved on the same basis as section 4 and supported by sufficient evidence. There is no exemption authority over the section 8 prohibitions. Material amendments to the Policy are approved by the Risk, Compliance and ESG Committee.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Officers and their Close Associates are prohibited from ... entering into any financial arrangements whereby a security interest is granted in respect of any vested VCX Securities which remain subject to a trading restriction or forfeiture condition.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The prohibition on granting security is deliberately confined to vested-but-restricted securities, so a security interest over freely held vested securities is not prohibited, which is what makes a funded collar arguable at Vicinity.

bespoke_clauses.clause: entering into arrangements properly described as margin lending arrangements in relation to VCX securities, which may include entering into a margin lending arrangement in respect of VCX securities, transferring VCX securities into an existing margin loan account and selling VCX securities held in an existing margin loan account.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: 'Properly described as margin lending arrangements' is narrower than a general secured financing ban, so a bilateral term loan with a fixed advance and no maintenance margin is arguably outside it, but the facility must be structured and documented so it is not in substance a margin loan.

bespoke_clauses.clause: VCX securities: Any Securities of Vicinity Centres and any derivatives entered into with a third party over or in relation to any VCX securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The put and call written by the bank are themselves VCX securities, so entry, roll, unwind and settlement each require the dual approvals and must fall outside a blackout period.

bespoke_clauses.topic: hedging ban tied to remuneration status
bespoke_clauses.clause: hedging or entering into an arrangement that would have the effect of limiting their exposure to risk relating to an element of their remuneration that is unvested, or which remains subject to a trading restriction or forfeiture condition
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The collar may only be written over securities that have vested and are free of any trading restriction or forfeiture condition, so the bank must diligence clawback and holding-lock terms in the plan documents, not just vesting.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The section 7 exclusions from the blackout restrictions cover only plan option exercises, takeover acceptances and transfers out of the employee share plan trust with no change in beneficial ownership.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike Ramsay or MinRes, Vicinity has no exclusion for a disposal resulting from a secured lender exercising its rights, so enforcement or physical settlement during a blackout period would be an unexcused dealing and a Policy breach.

bespoke_clauses.clause: short-term dealing (i.e. if a person buys (or sells) VCX securities on a date and then sells (or buys) any VCX securities on a date that is less than 30 days after the first dealing)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The test compares any two dealings in any VCX securities, and derivatives count, so the option legs and any share dealing must be spaced at least 30 days apart and settlement must not follow a recent acquisition.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Chairman – approval from both the Chairman of the Audit Committee and the CEO; Other Directors – both the Chairman of the Board and the CEO; CEO – both the Chairman of the Board and the Chief Legal, Risk & ESG Officer or Group Company Secretary; All other Restricted Officers – any two of the CEO, Chief Legal, Risk & ESG Officer or the Group Company Secretary.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Two approvers are required for every leg, which lengthens lead time and means the structure must be explained to Board-level approvers before pricing.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A written response to a trading request should be given within two business days of the initial request. Trading by a Restricted Officer may be conducted no more than five business days after the trading request has been approved. ... Any trading request can be approved or not approved without giving reasons and can be withdrawn by email if new information comes to light or there is a change in circumstances.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Pricing and execution must complete within five business days of approval, and approval can be withdrawn by email at any point before the trade, which the bank must accommodate as a condition precedent.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A decision not to approve a trading request is final and binding on the individual seeking approval. A refusal to approve a trading request is confidential information and must not be disclosed to anyone.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no appeal, and the executive cannot tell the bank why a leg has been blocked, so the documents should not require the client to explain a refusal.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the intention of this Policy not only to minimise the risk of insider trading but also to avoid the appearance of insider trading and the significant reputational damage that may cause
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Approval turns partly on appearances, so a collar over a large proportion of a director's holding is likely to be refused even where technically permitted.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any trustee of a trust or other fiduciary arrangement under which the Restricted Officer, their spouse or partner or their dependent children, are or may be a beneficiary; and any company in which the Restricted Officer, or any of the above-mentioned persons, directly or indirectly holds a majority of the shares or otherwise controls or significantly influences.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The 'may be a beneficiary' and 'significantly influences' limbs are wide, so almost any family holding vehicle used as borrower or collar counterparty is itself bound by the section 8 prohibitions and the approval regime.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Vicinity, Vicinity Centres or the Group means the stapled group of Vicinity Limited and Vicinity Centres Trust, of which Vicinity Centres RE Ltd is the responsible entity; 'securities' includes any unit or other interest in the scheme.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The underlying is a stapled security comprising a share and a trust unit, so the collar confirmations and the security documents must describe the stapled security correctly and deal with a possible destapling.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This Policy also applies to employees on extended leave from Vicinity, including parental leave, personal leave, long service leave, a career break or leave without pay.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Time away from the business does not suspend the approval requirements or the section 8 prohibitions for the life of the collar.

summary: A funded collar is arguable at Vicinity but only over securities that have vested and are free of any trading restriction or forfeiture condition, and it requires careful structuring of the loan. Section 8 imposes three absolute, approval-proof bans on Restricted Officers and their Close Associates: hedging anything that is unvested, restricted or forfeitable; granting a security interest over vested securities that remain restricted or forfeitable; and entering into arrangements properly described as margin lending arrangements. Neither the security interest ban nor the margin lending ban reaches a bilateral term loan secured on freely held vested securities, so the funded leg is available if the facility is genuinely not a margin loan, has no maintenance margin, and is documented as such. The option legs are themselves VCX securities because the definition captures derivatives entered into with a third party, so entry, roll and unwind each need two named approvers (Chairman of the Board and CEO for a director), a written response within two business days, execution within five, notification to the Company Secretary within two business days of the trade and, for directors, an ASX report, all outside the 30 June and 31 December blackouts and any email-notified extension. Two risks stand out: there is no exclusion for a disposal by a secured lender exercising its rights, so enforcement or physical settlement in a blackout would breach the Policy, and the 30-day short-term dealing test compares any two dealings in any VCX securities, derivatives included.
